Subject: Sudden launch spike — immediate throttle increase + overrun pricing?

Hi Rafael,

We just flipped a marketing campaign live and are seeing an immediate 3x traffic spike to our API endpoints. Our app is returning a lot of 429s and we need a short, immediate throughput increase for the next ~72 hours to avoid customer-impacting errors.

Can Redwood do a temporary rate-limit bump to handle a sustained +3x for up to 72 hours? If so, please confirm:
- What provisional pricing will apply for the overrun tokens during that window?
- Do you require a PO or prepayment for the temporary uplift?
- How fast can this be activated? We need something within the next 2–4 hours if possible.

Attached: fastretail_usage_report_Mar-Apr.csv (sample traffic and token counts).

If we have to pay a surcharge we can do that — but we also want to understand what concessions are available if we convert to a committed plan following this launch. We do have procurement timelines and can sign a 12-month commit if pricing is reasonable.

Thanks — we’re on standby.

—Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Ops, FastRetail
ops@fastretail.com

Priya — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the usage file. Sorry you’re seeing 429s. We can absolutely support an expedited, short-term uplift; a few clarifying Qs so we pick the right approach:

- From the CSV you sent: is the expected extra volume ~18M tokens over 72 hours (peaks ~450k tokens/hour)? Confirm if that’s peak sustained or bursty.
- Do you need per-minute concurrency increases or per-second QPS? (We can tune both but pricing differs.)

Provisional plan I’m escalating to Ops/Pricing right now (I’ll keep this thread):
- 72-hour provisional uplift to +3x throttle, immediate activation (we can target within 90 minutes once PO/approval path is decided).
- Provisional surcharge: 1.8x your base per-token rate for uplifted consumption. This is a temporary uplift rate we give while we evaluate commit incentives.
- If you convert to a 12-month commit within 30 days, we’ll credit back up to 50% of the surcharge (applied as a one-time invoice credit).

I’ve looped in Laura (pricing) and Ben (account exec) to finalize exact numbers and DocuSign flow. If you can confirm the expected extra tokens/hour and whether procurement can issue a PO today, we’ll push for same-day activation.

Rafael Mendes

Hi Priya — thanks for the details and for flagging procurement availability. I own pricing here; outlined below is a concrete, time-limited proposal to enable the uplift immediately while protecting both sides from runaway charges.

Provisional uplift offer (72 hours):
- Uplift activation: immediate (Ops will flip the throttle once we have PO confirmation).
- Rate model options:
  1) Emergency surcharge (recommended for speed): per-token uplift at 1.8x your current base rate, billed for any consumption above your committed tiers for the 72-hour window. No prepayment required if we get an emergency PO.
  2) Pay-as-you-go uplift: per-token uplift at 1.2x base rate, with a hard cap at +40% above your reported baseline spend; any consumption beyond cap reverts to 1.8x. Requires a short contract addendum to align terms.
- Commitment incentive: sign a 12-month commit (min ARR threshold included in Doc) within 30 days and receive a one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of uplift surcharges incurred during this 72-hour window, up to $25,000.
- Activation SLA: we will target activation within 90 minutes of receiving emergency PO or explicit written approval in this thread.

Attachments: provisional-uplift-terms-FastRetail-v1.pdf (contains legal appendix and activation checklist). DocuSign link will be provided; we can also accept an emailed PO for same-day activation.

Next steps:
- Priya: confirm whether you want option 1 (fastest) or option 2 (lower surcharge but requires addendum).
- If option 1: send emergency PO to billing@redwood.example.com and we’ll start the activation runbook.
- Ben: please prep the DocuSign with proposal language and the credit path tied to FR-2027-0426.

Laura Bennett
